title: Cardiopulmonary Complications of Electronic Cigarettes
summary: The study aims to look at whether changes in the blood vessels of the lungs are related to how well electronic cigarette users tolerate exercise. It also aims to investigate whether increasing blood flow to the lungs can improve the reduced ability of E-CIG users' lungs to transfer oxygen into the bloodstream.

interventions.name: Lower body positive and negative pressure

criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

Adolescent Cohort:

1. Participants aged ≥12 and \<18 years
2. Non-smoking and Non-E-CIG Use: \<100 lifetime cigarettes and \< 200 E-CIG puffs
3. E-CIG Use Only: currently using E-CIGs every day or some days
4. Cannabis Use: cannabis smoking history of \> 1 joint-year
5. Combined E-CIG and Cannabis Use: adolescents who meet both #3 and #4

Adult Cohort:

1. Participants aged 18-40 years
2. Non-smoking and Non-E-CIG Use: \<100 lifetime cigarettes and \< 200 E-CIG puffs
3. E-CIG Use Only: currently using E-CIGs every day or some days
4. Cannabis Use: cannabis smoking history of \> 1 joint-year
5. Combined E-CIG and Cannabis Use: adults who meet both #3 and #4

Exclusion Criteria:

1. Contraindication to pulmonary function testing (i.e. recent thoracic or abdominal surgery, aneurysms, cardiovascular instability)
2. Unable to provide informed consent
3. Currently undergoing treatment for lung cancer
4. Cigarette smoking in the past 6 months
5. Physician-diagnosed chronic lung disease (e.g. cystic fibrosis, asthma, primary ciliary dyskinesia, bronchopulmonary dysplasia) (adolescent arm only)
6. Self-reported premature infancy, referring to individuals who were born premature (born before the 37th week of pregnancy). Previous literature and work in our lab have shown that lung development is blunted in these individuals, and we are therefore excluding those born prematurely so that underdeveloped lungs do not impact the findings of the present study.
7. Pregnancy. To confirm this, women not using contraception will be given a pregnancy test prior to starting the study. Pregnancy presents additional complications and may confound the results of the study; therefore, pregnant women will be excluded.
